name: Peter Ozo-Eson
detail: Former NLC Chief Economist and General Secretary (2014-2019) who called in January 2015 for taxing private jets and luxury goods of the rich at a very high rate; passed away on 13 December 2025. The institutional position is recorded under Nigeria Labour Congress (A0041).

name: Taiwo Oyedele
detail: Chairman of the Presidential Fiscal Policy and Tax Reforms Committee; despite frequent 'tax the fruit, not the seed' and progressive taxation framing, the 2024-2025 tax reform bills (Nigeria Tax Act 2025) raise the top Personal Income Tax marginal rate to 25% and reform Capital Gains Tax and VAT rather than introducing a net wealth tax, and explicitly avoid taxing capital stock.

name: Bola Ahmed Tinubu
detail: President of Nigeria; transmitted the four 2024 Tax Reform Bills enacted into the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 (effective January 2026), which reform income, capital gains, and value-added taxation without creating a net wealth tax.

name: Ireti Kingibe
detail: Labour Party Senator for the Federal Capital Territory; criticized the 25% top marginal rate in the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 in a viral video and argued against taxing struggling citizens, without clearly proposing a wealth tax in the opened sources.

name: Giovanni Occhiali, Jalia Kangave, and Hamza Ahmed Khan
detail: Authors of the July 2024 ICTD study 'Taxing High Net Worth Individuals in Nigeria: Preliminary Insights and the Case of Borno State' (ICTD Research in Brief 132 / Working Paper 188), which analyses Personal Income Tax compliance among HNWIs under State Boards of Internal Revenue rather than advocating a net wealth tax.

name: Ayuba Wabba
detail: Former President of the Nigeria Labour Congress; led an October 2016 NLC tax justice march to the Ministry of Finance in Abuja demanding action against multinational corporate tax evasion, Panama Papers offshore tax havens, and illicit financial flows rather than a domestic wealth tax.

name: Ene Obi
detail: Former Country Director of ActionAid Nigeria; spoke at the October 2021 National Tax Summit in Abuja calling for fiscal accountability, curbing tax leakages, and reducing public debt borrowing, without explicitly proposing a wealth tax in the opened report.

name: Isaac Botti
detail: Social Action Programmes Coordinator who presented the December 2023 TJ&GP/CISLAC/Christian Aid report 'Tax Expenditures and Its Implications on Debt Management and Sustainability in Nigeria' calling for carbon and pollution taxes and curbing multinational corporate tax waivers.
